angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 219,493 km at 10.61 pc = 0.28 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 94.2664 +/- 0.0155 mas (same row, RUWE 1.27): 10.61 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.3155 +/- 0.0062 solar radii from Cadieux et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of L 98-59 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..154C/abstract): 219,493 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.2923 +/- 0.0067 solar masses from Cadieux et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of L 98-59 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..154C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3415 +/- 60 K from Cadieux et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of L 98-59 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..154C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Cadieux et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of L 98-59 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..154C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/l-98-59.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.906, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
